'''''Selenicereus undatus''''', the '''white-fleshed pitahaya''', is a species of the genus ''[[Selenicereus]]'' (formerly ''Hylocereus'') in the family [[Cactaceae]]<ref name="EoFN"/> and is the most cultivated species in the genus. It is used both as an ornamental vine and as a fruit crop, the '''[[pitahaya]]''' or '''[[:simple:Dragon_fruit|dragon fruit]]'''.<ref name="แก้วมังกร">นิดดา หงส์วิวัฒน์ และทวีทอง หงส์วิวัฒน์. แก้วมังกร ใน ผลไม้ 111 ชนิด: คุณค่าอาหารและการกิน. กทม. แสงแดด. 2550 หน้า 37 - 39</ref>

Like all true [[cactus|cacti]], the genus originates in the [[Americas]]. ''S. undatus'' is native from Mexico to Honduras;{{r|powo}}<ref>{{cite web | url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/selenicereus-undatus/ | title=Selenicereus undatus (Belle-Of-The-Night, Cinderella Plant, Dragon Fruit, Dragon Fruit Tree, Honolulu Queen, Jesus in the Cradle, Moonflower, Moonlight Cactus, Nightblooming Cactus, Night Blooming Cereus, Pitahya Plant, Pitaya, Queen of the Night, Red Pitaya, Strawberry-Pear) | North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox }}</ref> it may be a [[hybrid (biology)|hybrid]].{{cn|date=August 2025}}

== Description ==
[[File:Dragonfruit Chiayi market.jpg|thumb|The red [[pitahaya]] at the Chiayi market, [[Taiwan]]]]
[[File:Hylocereus undatus 111.JPG|220px|thumb|right|The flowers in Rome]]

=== Plant ===
The stems are scandent (climbing habit), creeping, sprawling or clambering, and branch profusely. There can be four to seven stems, between {{cvt|5 and 10|m}} or longer, with joints from {{cvt|30 to 120|cm}} or longer, and {{cvt|10 to 12|cm}} thick; with generally three ribs; margins are corneous (horn-like) with age, and undulate.<ref name="แก้วมังกร"/>

[[Areoles]], that is, the small area bearing spines or hairs on a cactus, are {{cvt|2|mm}} across with internodes {{cvt|1 to 4|cm}}. Spines on the adult branches are {{cvt|1 to 4|mm}} long, being acicular (needle-like) to almost conical, and greyish brown to black in colour and spreading, with a deep green epidermis.<ref name="แก้วมังกร"/>

=== Flowers ===
The scented, nocturnal flowers are {{cvt|25 to 30|cm}} long, {{cvt|15 to 17|cm}} wide with the [[pericarpel]] {{cvt|2.5 to 5|cm}} long, about {{cvt|2.5|cm}} thick, bracteoles ovate, acute, to 2.5 to less than {{cvt|4|cm}} long; receptacle about {{cvt|3|cm}} thick, bracteoles are linear-lanceolate, {{cvt|3 to 8|cm}} long; outer [[tepals]] lanceolate-linear to linear, acuminate (tapering to a point), being {{cvt|10 to 15|cm}} long, {{cvt|10 to 15|mm}} wide and mucronate (ending in a short sharp point). Their colour is greenish-yellow or whitish, rarely rose-tinged; these outer tepals, or [[sepals]], are about 65 in number, and bring the flower to a total width of up to {{cvt|35|cm|in|0}}.<ref>Reisigl, World of Flowers, loc.cit.</ref> The inner tepals are lanceolate (tapering to a point at the tip) to oblanceolate (i.e. more pointed at the base), up to {{cvt|10 to 15|cm}} long about {{cvt|40|mm}} wide at widest point, and mucronate, unbroken, sharp to acuminate (pointed), and white.

File:HPIM0069.JPG|Blooming flower

Stamens {{cvt|5 to 10|cm}} long, are declinate, inserted in one continuous zone from throat to {{cvt|35|mm}} above the pericarpel and cream. The style (bearing the stigma) to 17, they are {{cvt|5 to 24.5|cm}} long, stout, {{cvt|6 to 8|mm}} thick, cream, and up to 26 stigma lobes, they can be whole or sometimes split at the top, cream, about {{cvt|25|mm}} long. Nectar chambers are {{cvt|30|mm}} long.<ref name="แก้วมังกร"/>

=== Fruit ===
[[File:Caryophyllales - Hylocereus undatus - 3.jpg|thumb|130px|Mature fruit]]
The fruit is oblong to oval, {{cvt|6 to 12|cm}} long, {{cvt|4 to 9|cm}} thick, red with large [[bracteole]]s, with white, or more uncommonly, pink pulp and edible black seeds.<ref name="แก้วมังกร"/>

== Habitat ==
''Selenicereus undatus'' is [[lithophytic]] or [[hemiepiphytic]]. It is widely distributed through the tropics in cultivation. It is a sprawling or vining, terrestrial or epiphytic cactus. They climb by use of aerial roots and can reach a height of {{convert|10|m|ft|abbr=off|sp=us}} or more growing on rocks and trees.

== Systematics ==
This species is closely related to ''S. ocamponis'' and ''S. escuintlensis''. ''Selenicereus undatus'' was described by (Haw.) Britton & Rose and published in Flora of Bermuda 256. 1918. In 2017, D. R. Hunt groups the genus ''Hylocereus'' within the genus ''Selenicereus''. This has been supported by a phylogenetic analysis of the tribe Hylocereeae (Korotkova, et al., 2017), therefore this species is now treated under the name ''Selenicereus undatus''<ref name=POWO_30011812-2>{{cite web |title=''Selenicereus'' Britton & Rose |work=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:30011812-2 |access-date=2021-03-03 }}</ref>

=== Taxonomy ===
The species epithet ''undatus'' in [[Latin]] means "wavy" from ''unda'' "wave",<ref>{{cite dictionary |url=https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0059:entry=unda|title=unda |last1= Lewis |first1= Charlton T. |last2= Short |first2= Charles |dictionary= A Latin Dictionary |publisher= Perseus Digital Library |date = 1879 }}</ref> referring to the wavy edges of its branch ribs.
